Rashi on Pesachim 11b:10:1.hebrew: אחד אמר בשנים בחדש - הרג זה את הנפש, ואחד מן העדים אומר בשלשה בחדש — עדותן קיימת. ובית דין היו בודקין אותן בשבע חקירות, כדלקמן. וכיון דהושוו שניהן לומר בשלישי או ברביעי, וכשבדקום איזה יום בחדש אמר זה בשני וזה אמר בשלישי — שניהן על יום אחד העידו, אלא שזה ידע בעיבורו של חודש, שחודש שעבר מלא והוקבע ר"ח ביום שלשים ואחד, וזה שאמר בשנים בחדש ידע בו, וזה שאמר שלשה סבור שהוקבע החדש ביום שלשים. והואיל ויש טועין בכך, אע"פ שמצווין אנו לחלק את עדותן כדי שתבטל להציל את הנפש — אין בידינו כח לחלקו:
Rashi on Pesachim 11b:10:1.english: One said: On the second of the month - [that] this [person] killed the victim, and one of the witnesses says: "[It was] on the third of the month" — their testimony is valid. And the court would examine them with the seven inquiries, as [explained] below. And since both of them agreed in saying [that it occurred] on the third or on the fourth [day of the week], and when they examined them [as to] which day of the month [it was], this one said on the second and that one said on the third — both of them were testifying about one [and the same] day. Rather, this one knew of the intercalation of the month — that the previous month was full, and Rosh Chodesh was established on the thirty-first day, and this [witness] who said "on the second of the month" knew of it; while that [witness] who said "[the] third" assumed that the [new] month was established on the thirtieth day. And since people [commonly] err in this regard, even though we are commanded to differentiate their testimony so that it will be invalidated [in order] to save the life [of the accused], we do not have the power to differentiate it.

Rashi on Pesachim 11b:12:1.hebrew: עדותן בטלה - דבהא ליכא למטעי. וקרא כתיב (דברים יג): "ודרשת וחקרת והנה אמת נכון" — שתהא עדותן מכוונת. ואי לא, לא קטלינן; והוא והן פטורים, דאין עדים נהרגין אלא על ידי הזמה:
Rashi on Pesachim 11b:12:1.english: Their testimony is void - For in this [case] one cannot make a mistake. And Scripture writes (Deuteronomy 13:15): "Then you shall inquire, and search... and, behold, if it be truth, and the thing certain" — that their testimony must be aligned. And if not, we do not execute [the accused]; and [both] he and they are exempt, for witnesses are not executed except through hazamah [conspiracy].

Rashi on Pesachim 11b:12:2.english: One says at two hours, etc., their testimony is valid - For a person errs by that much.

Rashi on Pesachim 11b:13:1.hebrew: אחד אומר בחמש ואחד אומר בשבע עדותן בטלה - אפילו לר' יהודה, דבחמש חמה במזרחו של רקיע, ויכול להבין על ידי הצל — כשנותן ידו כנגד המזרח, הוה הצל לצד מערב:
Rashi on Pesachim 11b:13:1.english: [If] one says at five and one says at seven, their testimony is void - [This applies] even according to Rabbi Yehuda. For at five [hours], the sun is in the eastern [part] of the sky, and one can discern [this] by means of the shadow — when one places his hand opposite the east, the shadow is toward the west.

Rashi on Pesachim 11b:13:2.english: And at seven [hours], the sun is in the west - And the shadow is toward the east.

Rashi on Pesachim 11b:14:1.hebrew: כשתמצא לומר - כשתדקדק בדבריהם ותעמוד על מכונו, תמצא: לדברי רבי מאיר — דמקיים עדות דב' וג' ומבטל של ג' ושל ה' — אין אדם טועה ולא כלום; ולדברי ר' יהודה — דמקיים אף שלש וחמש — אדם טועה חצי שעה. לר' מאיר אין אדם טועה כלום, והטועה שקרן הוא. והאי דמקיים ר' מאיר עדות של שתים ושלש — משום ששניהם העידו על רגע אחד, דמעשה כי הוה במיפק תרתי ומעייל תלת, ביציאתה של שניה כשהשלישית נכנסת, ושניהן כך העידו: דהאי דאמר שתים — בסוף שניה קאמר, והאי דקאמר כו'. ולקמן פריך: מי יודע שכוונתן לכך היתה? דילמא האי דקאמר שתים — בתחלת שתים קאמר, ויש חילוק ביניהן, והואיל ולר"מ אין תולין בטעות — הרי הן שקרנין:
Rashi on Pesachim 11b:14:1.english: When you analyze the matter - When you examine their words closely and understand [the matter] properly, you will find: According to the words of Rabbi Meir — who upholds testimony of [one witness saying] two and [one saying] three, and invalidates [testimony] of three and five — a person does not err at all; and according to the words of Rabbi Yehuda — who upholds even [testimony of] three and five — a person errs [by up to] half an hour. According to Rabbi Meir, a person does not err at all, and one who errs is a liar. And this [fact] that Rabbi Meir upholds testimony of [one saying] two and [one saying] three is because both of them testified about a single moment — for when the incident occurred, [it was] as the second [hour] departed and the third entered, at the departure of the second as the third was entering, and both of them testified accordingly: for this [witness] who said "two" meant at the end of the second, and that [witness] who said, etc. [i.e., "three", meant at the beginning of the third]. And later on [the Gemara] challenges: Who knows that this was their intention? Perhaps this [witness] who said "two" meant at the beginning of the second, and there is a discrepancy between them, and since according to Rabbi Meir we do not attribute [discrepancies] to error, they are liars.

Rashi on Pesachim 11b:14:2.hebrew: ולדברי רבי יהודה תולין בטעות חצי שעה - הילכך, כי אמר האי בשלש והאי בחמש עדותן קיימת, דמעשה כי הוה — בפלגא דארבע וכו', וזה אמר בסוף שלש וזה בתחלת חמש, וכל אחד מהן טעה מן המעשה חצי שעה. ולקמיה פריך ליה: היכי מהדרינן לצרופי עדותן? הוה לן למימר דהאי בתחלת ג' קאמר והאי בסוף חמש קאמר, ויש חילוק גדול ביניהן, וכולי האי לא טעו, ותחלק עדותן ונציל את הנפש:
Rashi on Pesachim 11b:14:2.english: And according to the statement of Rabbi Yehuda, we attribute [it] to an error of half an hour - Therefore, when this [witness] says at three [hours] and that [witness] says at five, their testimony is valid, for when the incident occurred, [it was] at the midpoint of the fourth [hour], etc., and this [witness] said at the end of the third [hour], and that [witness] at the beginning of the fifth [hour], and each one of them erred from [the actual time of] the incident by half an hour. And later, [the Gemara] objects to him: How can we seek to combine their testimony? We ought to say that this [witness] said [it occurred] at the beginning of the third [hour], and that [witness] said at the end of the fifth [hour], and there is a great discrepancy between them, and [people] do not err to such an extent, so their testimony should be divided, and we should save the life [of the accused].

Rashi on Pesachim 11b:16:1.hebrew: וחד מנייהו קא טעי משהו - אם בסוף שתים הוה, האי דקאמר שלש — בתחלת שלש, וקאי טעי משהו; ואי בתחלת ג', האי דקאמר שתים — בסוף שתים, וקא טעי משהו:
Rashi on Pesachim 11b:16:1.english: And one of them errs a bit - If [the incident] occurred at the end of the second [hour], the one who said "three" [meant] at the beginning of the third, and he errs by a bit; and if [it occurred] at the beginning of the third, the one who said "two" [meant] at the end of the second, and he errs by a bit.

Rashi on Pesachim 11b:16:2.hebrew: לדברי רבי יהודה - מעשה הוה בסוף שלש, והאי דאמר בתחילת חמש — טעי שעה רביעית ומשהו של סוף שלש. אי נמי, בתחילת חמש הוה, והאי דאמר בסוף שלש — טעה שעה רביעית ומשהו:
Rashi on Pesachim 11b:16:2.english: According to Rabbi Yehuda - The incident occurred at the end of the third [hour], and this [witness] who said [it was] at the beginning of the fifth [hour] erred [by] the fourth hour and a bit of the end of the third [hour]. Alternatively, it occurred at the beginning of the fifth [hour], and this [witness] who said [it was] at the end of the third [hour] erred [by] the fourth hour and a bit.

Rashi on Pesachim 11b:1:1.english: About his property - This priest is anxious about the firstborn, lest it die.

Rashi on Pesachim 11b:2:1.hebrew: כ"ש - הואיל ובהול הוא, אי לא שרית ליה במקום שאינו עושה בו מום — עובר על דבריך ועושה, ושוב אין נזהר בין מקום מום לשלא במקום מום, דסבור שהכל שוה:
Rashi on Pesachim 11b:2:1.english: All the more so - Since he is anxious [about losing his animal], if you do not permit him [to let blood] in a place where it does not cause a blemish, he will transgress your words and do [so anyway]; and thereafter he will not be careful [to distinguish] between a place of a blemish and a place not of a blemish, since he will think that it is all the same.

Rashi on Pesachim 11b:3:1.english: [One may] scrape - [This is Old French:] estrillid [to currycomb].

Rashi on Pesachim 11b:3:2.hebrew: מקרצפין - כדפרשינן: בכלי ששיניו גסות, ואינו עושה חבורה — דחובל בבעלי חיים אב מלאכה היא. קתני מיהת "אבל מקרצפין", אלמא לא גזר: מתוך שאדם בהול, אי שרית ליה קירצוף — עביד קידור, לפי שהטיט מכחיש את הבהמה ומצערה:
Rashi on Pesachim 11b:3:2.english: One may scratch - As we explained: with an implement whose teeth are thick, and it does not inflict a wound — for wounding a living creature is a primary category of labor. In any event, it teaches: “However, one may scratch,” evidently [showing that] he did not decree: Since a person is anxious [about his property], if you permit scratching to him he will perform scraping — [an anxiety that exists] because the mud weakens the animal and causes it pain.

Rashi on Pesachim 11b:6:1.english: Not interchanged - And the Rabbis hold [that] it is interchanged.

Rashi on Pesachim 11b:7:1.hebrew: ושורפין בתחלת שש - ואע"ג דכל שעה ששית מדאורייתא שריא, גזור רבנן עלה, דילמא טעי וסבור על השביעי' שהיא ששית. אבל אחמישי' לא טעי למימר על השביעית שהיא חמישית, ומותר:
Rashi on Pesachim 11b:7:1.english: And one burns [it] at the beginning of the sixth [hour] - And even though the entire sixth hour is permitted by Torah law, the Sages decreed regarding it, lest one err and think of the seventh [hour] that it is the sixth. But regarding the fifth [hour], one will not err to say of the seventh [hour] that it is the fifth, and [therefore eating then is] permitted.

Rashi on Pesachim 11b:7:2.hebrew: תולין כל חמש - ואינו אוכל, דטעי וסבור על שביעית שהיא חמישית. ומיהו, לשרוף אינו צריך, ומאכיל לבהמתו. אבל ששית — אף בהנאה אסור מדרבנן, גזירה משום שביעית:
Rashi on Pesachim 11b:7:2.english: One places it in abeyance the entire fifth [hour] - And one does not eat [it], for one might err and think regarding the seventh [hour] that it is the fifth [hour]. But nevertheless, one does not need to burn [it], and one may feed [it] to one’s animal. But [during] the sixth [hour], even deriving benefit is rabbinically forbidden, as a decree on account of the seventh [hour].

Rashi on Pesachim 11b:8:2.english: Of a thanks-offering [that are] disqualified - And in the Gemara it explains who disqualified them.

Rashi on Pesachim 11b:8:3.english: Were placed - On every Passover eve.

Rashi on Pesachim 11b:8:4.hebrew: על גב האיצטבא - סטיו שהיה בהר הבית, ששם מתקבצין ויושבין בני אדם, והיו רואין אותן לסימן:
Rashi on Pesachim 11b:8:4.english: On top of the bench - A colonnade that was on the Temple Mount, where people would gather and sit, and they would see them as a sign.

Rashi on Pesachim 11b:8:5.hebrew: ניטלה אחת מהן - בתחלת חמש, בא שליח בית דין ונוטל האחת:
Rashi on Pesachim 11b:8:5.english: One of them was taken - At the beginning of the fifth [hour], an agent of the court comes and takes the one [loaf].

Rashi on Pesachim 11b:9:1.hebrew: ותרומה כל חמש - דאסור להפסיד קדשים בידים, כל זמן שיכול לאוכלן:
Rashi on Pesachim 11b:9:1.english: And teruma [during] the entire fifth [hour] - For it is forbidden to actively cause the loss of consecrated foods, as long as one is able to eat them.

Rashi on Pesachim 11b:9:2.english: And one burns at the beginning of the sixth [hour] - For surely most [people] err between the sixth and the seventh [hour].

Tosafot on Pesachim 11b:11:1.hebrew: זה ידע בעיבורו של חדש - וה"ה דה"מ למימר: זה ידע בחסרונו של חדש וזה לא ידע, דחדש שעבר חסר היה. והקשה ריב"א: ומה אלו דייקינן בהני סהדי דתרוייהו ידעי בעיבורו של חדש, וה"ל עדות מוכחשת, ואיך ניקום וניקטול מספיקא?! דהכי פריך בסמוך. אע"ג דבפ' בן סורר (סנהד' סט.) דייק מהכא דרובא דאינשי עבידי דטעי בעיבורא דירחא — מ"מ מה נפסיד אם נדקדק בהם? וי"ל דהכא דייקינן בהו שפיר, כיון דשיילי להו באיזה יום, וקמיכווני ליום אחד — ש"מ שזה לא ידע. ומ"מ שפיר מוכיח בבן סורר (שם) מהכא דאזלינן בתר רובא בדיני נפשות, דרובא טעי בעיבורא דירחא; דאי לא אזלי' בתר רובא, כיון שזה אומר בשנים וזה אומר בשלשה — מיד ה"ל מוכחשין, וכי הדר מכוונים ליום אחד ה"ל חוזר ומגיד. תדע, דהא אחד אומר בג' ואחד אומר בה' עדותן בטלה, אע"פ שמכוונים ליום אחד, ולא אמרינן דטעו בשני עיבורים, דבתרי עיבורי לא טעו אינשי, וחשבינן להו חוזר ומגיד:
Tosafot on Pesachim 11b:11:1.english: "This [witness] knows about the addition of an extra day to the month" - And the same applies [such] that [the mishna] could have said: "This [witness] knows about the deficiency of the month, and that [witness] does not know [about it]," for the previous month was defective [i.e., lasted twenty-nine days]. And the Riva asked: But what if we were to examine these witnesses and [find] that both of them knew about the addition of an extra day to the month? Then it would be contradictory testimony, and how could we arise and execute [the accused] based on uncertainty?! For so [the Gemara] objects nearby [12a]. Even though in the chapter [entitled] Ben Sorer (Sanhedrin 69a) [the Gemara] infers from here that most people are apt to err regarding the addition of an extra day to the month, nevertheless, what would we lose if we examine them closely? And one can say that here we indeed examine them well: since we ask them, "On which day [of the week did it occur]?" and they agree on the same day, deduce from this that this [witness] did not know [about the addition of an extra day]. And nevertheless, [the Gemara] in Ben Sorer (ibid.) correctly proves from here that we follow the majority in capital cases, for the majority err regarding the addition of an extra day to the month; for if we did not follow the majority, then since this [witness] says on the second [of the month] and that [witness] says on the third, they would immediately be [considered] contradicted, and when they subsequently agree on the same day, it would be [disqualified as] retracting and altering their testimony [chozer umaggid]. Know [that this is so], for where one says on the third and one says on the fifth, their testimony is void even though they agree on the same day, and we do not say that they erred regarding two additions of an extra day, because people do not err regarding two additions, and we consider them as having retracted and altered their testimony.

Tosafot on Pesachim 11b:12:1.hebrew: אחד אומר בשתי שעות - וא"ת: אמאי עדותן קיימת? אילו דייקינן בהני סהדי, הא דקאמר שתים — בתחילת שתים, וה"ל קודם הנץ החמה, ועדותן בטלה, כדאמר לקמן — דתחילת שעה שניה קודם הנץ החמה הוא, דמהלך אדם ביום עשר פרסה, שהן מ' מילין, ומעלות השחר עד הנץ החמה מהלך ה' מילין, כדאמר במי שהיה טמא (לקמן פסחים צג:), וזה עולה לשעה ומחצה! וי"ל: כשזה אומר קודם הנץ החמה וזה אומר לאחר הנץ החמה, דמדקדקין בהנץ — לא טעו אינשי; אבל הני לא דקדקו אלא בשעות, ואין בני אדם בקיאין בשעות, וסבורין שהשניה התחילה אחר הנץ החמה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 11b:12:1.english: "One says at two hours" - And if you say: Why is their testimony valid? Were we to examine these witnesses closely, this [witness] who says "two" [might mean] at the beginning of the second [hour], and it would [thus] be prior to sunrise, and their testimony would be void, as [the Gemara] says below! For the beginning of the second hour is prior to sunrise — as a person's walking [distance] in a day is ten parasangs, which are forty mil, and from dawn until sunrise is a walk of five mil, as [the Gemara] says in [the chapter entitled] Mi Shehayah Tamei (below, Pesachim 93b), and this amounts to an hour and a half. And one can say [in resolution]: When this [witness] says "prior to sunrise" and that [witness] says "after sunrise," since [people] are precise regarding sunrise, people do not err; but these [witnesses] were precise only regarding hours, and people are not proficient in [calculating] the hours, and they assume that the second [hour] began after sunrise.
